name: Payroll and income records received
one_line: The employee-side payroll situation on the Finance schema: recurring pay statements, corrections, off-cycle payments, annual earnings summaries and employer-issued year-end income records received from one employer. It requires a payer/employee role structure plus pay-period or aggregate earnings evidence, recommends institution then tax_year then record_type, and keeps offers, bank credits, retirement-plan statements and employer-wide payroll runs on their own neighbouring templates.
design_cite: 00 names the legal Finance vocabulary exactly: “Finance files may use institution, account type, tax year, and record type.” It names the broader template world that permits this row as “financial records, travel, legal matters, creative projects, software repositories, personal administration, and photo collections” and states that “Each template should define the domain’s allowed fact fields, detection signals, recommended folder dimensions, preferred dimension order, optional branch patterns, privacy rules, and validation constraints.” 00 does not name payroll as its own organizational situation, so the payroll-specific boundaries and examples below are inference rather than design.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key_works: A pay statement normally identifies the interval whose earnings it reports, and that interval is the strongest distinction between a recurring payroll record and an offer, bank credit, annual tax form or account statement. creation_date is the timestamp of this file version, not the interval covered. tax_year is the tax role of a financial record, not a fortnightly or monthly pay period. The broader record_period key is the same cross-record proposal already made by finance.subscriptions-utilities; it avoids minting a private pay_period synonym and leaves R1c one shared proposal to adjudicate.
proposed_fields.note: Direct only from an explicit labelled Pay Period, Period Beginning/Ending, From/To or equivalent slot. A pay date, filename date, year-to-date column, email sent date or neighbouring statement does not fill it. It remains search/grouping metadata and never a folder level, because one branch per pay cycle would fragment the employer history.

deterministic: a PAY-STATEMENT structure on one evidence item: an employer or payer in a labelled issuer/header role, an employee or recipient block, an explicit pay-period or period-ending slot, and a gross-to-net table that labels earnings, taxes or deductions, and net pay. The roles and table structure are the signal; a company name plus an amount is not

an OFF-CYCLE, BONUS, COMMISSION, FINAL-PAY or CORRECTED-PAY statement that retains the same employer/recipient roles and gross, deduction and net slots, plus an explicit adjustment, correction, off-cycle or prior-statement reference. The lifecycle word alone is insufficient

an EMPLOYER ANNUAL EARNINGS structure: a labelled employer/payer block, a separate employee/recipient block, an explicit tax-year slot, and aggregate wage, withholding, pension or contribution slots. A jurisdiction-specific form name is only a record_type value supplied by the injected jurisdiction catalogue; no form name becomes a field or a dimension

a populated pay-history spreadsheet or structured export whose labelled columns jointly identify employer, pay-period start/end, gross earnings, taxes or other deductions, and net pay across recurring rows. A money column or a payroll-themed sheet name alone does not fire

an archive manifest, inspected without extraction, whose member names repeatedly carry pay-statement or payslip terms, coherent period-labelled filenames, and one employer token. The manifest may support a payroll-series candidate; it never copies member facts onto the archive
needs_llm: a multilingual or unfamiliar pay statement whose employer, recipient, pay-period and gross-to-net roles are visible but whose labels are not covered by the injected jurisdiction vocabulary. Under the Finance safety boundary, only a local or explicitly consented redacted dossier may be used, and the model must cite the bounded zones

a photographed, faxed or badly OCRed statement where rows are recovered but table alignment is broken. The model may decide whether the observed amounts play earnings, deduction and net roles; it must return unknown when it cannot reconstruct the labelled relationship

a statement mixing wages, expense reimbursement, leave, pension, insurance and equity lines. The model may identify the dominant pay-statement structure, but it may not activate every neighbouring template from a line item or create fields for those amounts

an employer-issued annual income statement that is also plausible support for a tax-filing packet. The file’s Finance facts stay the same; the model may only explain candidate group membership and cannot choose a permanent home or manufacture a tax_year from an unlabelled date

a sparse payroll-delivery email or portal notification whose attachment or linked record is absent. It may join a confirmed payroll series as a context-supported member, but the email does not inherit the employer, recipient, pay period or tax year from that group
never_alone: an employer, company, payroll bureau, payroll-product or government-authority name alone. The employer may be a payer, a prospective employer, a bank transaction counterparty or a plan sponsor; payroll-provider producer metadata never overrides the labelled employer/payer role

a currency amount, salary figure, withholding term, deduction name, year-to-date value or net-payment figure alone. The same evidence appears in offers, tax records, account statements, retirement-plan records, budgets and invoices
the words pay, paid, salary, wages, earnings, payroll, payslip, pay statement, bonus or commission in a filename or folder name. An unreadable file never gains a purpose from its filename
a pay date, month, year, pay-period-shaped string or recurring calendar event alone. tax_year requires its own explicit tax-year role, and record_period requires a labelled period slot

a masked tax, social-insurance, employee, bank or account identifier alone. Mask shapes recur across tax forms, bank records, payroll files and identity material and stay sensitive observations unless a declared field permits them
a bank deposit, repeated salary-description transaction or direct-deposit alert. A posted credit proves a bank transaction, not the gross-to-net payroll record that produced it
a spreadsheet, PDF, email, image, OCR result, archive, extension or source_type alone. File kind is a routing signal and cannot establish payroll meaning

an existing folder named Payroll, Payslips, Salary or Tax, a download session, or adjacency to an identified pay statement. Existing structure and session evidence can seed review, but cannot activate the template or write facts

missing EXIF or dense OCR text as proof that an image is a screenshot. A photographed payslip and a payroll-portal screenshot can carry the same words; capture evidence and payroll content must be evaluated separately

grouping_reasons: one employer-issued payroll history across recurring pay statements, off-cycle payments, corrections, final pay and the annual summary. The labelled employer/payer role anchors the group; a shared payroll bureau does not

one employer within one explicitly supported tax year. Statements without their own tax_year may join an accepted employer-year group as context-supported members, but the group never writes the missing tax_year onto them

one pay-period record across an original statement, correction and reissued copy. Content hash and version-family evidence distinguish a corrected version from an unrelated statement with the same pay date
one payroll-portal export packet containing statements, a pay-history export and a delivery notice. Sparse notices may join without inheriting institution, account_holder or record_period

one employer-issued year-end form may participate in both a payroll-history group and a tax-filing packet. Multi-membership preserves both organizational relationships; it does not change the file’s Finance facts or duplicate the bytes

different employers remain different payroll histories even when they use the same payroll bureau, tax authority or pension provider. The provider is a service/producer observation, not the institution value when the employer is explicitly labelled

template.why: institution leads because Pay Statement, Correction or Annual Summary is not intelligible until the paying employer is known, and one person may have several employers in one year. This applies 00’s rule that “a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” tax_year comes next only where its own explicit role is supported; it keeps a long employer history navigable without putting time first, because “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” record_type is the leaf separating recurring statements, corrections and annual records. account_type is omitted: ordinary payroll documents do not describe a financial account, and inventing Payroll as an account value would create a decorative one-child level. record_period remains metadata because a level for every pay cycle “creates a large number of tiny folders”; the canvas should “recommend flattening when a dimension does not materially improve retrieval.” Missing tax_year produces a shallower employer/record-type branch rather than an inferred year. The order is editable: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: An offer letter and a pay statement both carry an employer name beside a compensation figure. A labelled role title, future start date, proposed compensation and acceptance or countersignature block identifies recruiting; an employer/employee role pair plus a labelled pay period and gross, deduction and net rows identifies payroll actually received. The employer name and amount are shared evidence and cannot choose either template.

A pay statement and an employment record both name an employer, employee relationship and date. A recurring pay-period structure with gross-to-net rows belongs here; executed terms, onboarding, benefits election, performance, compensation-change or separation language describing the document itself belongs to employment records. A payroll deduction line does not turn the pay statement into every lifecycle document it mentions.

Payroll and bank-account records both carry organization names, masked identifiers, periods and money. A labelled employer/employee pair with a pay period and gross, deduction and net table belongs here; a labelled bank or card account with statement period, transactions and beginning/ending balance belongs to personal records. A direct-deposit authorization or salary credit is not a pay statement.

A pay statement’s year-to-date withholding and an employer year-end wage statement repeat employer, recipient and tax concepts. A labelled pay period with per-period gross-to-net rows is the recurring payroll discriminator; a tax-authority return, assessment, filing acknowledgement or numbered aggregate form with an explicit tax-year role is the tax-filing discriminator. A jurisdiction-specific employer year-end form can legitimately join both an employer payroll-history group and a tax-year packet, so the bare form alone must not cause facts or group membership to propagate in either direction.

A pay statement deduction line and a retirement-plan statement can both name an employer, employee contribution and employer contribution. A labelled pay period with gross, deductions and net pay belongs here; a labelled plan account, custodian and holdings, contribution-confirmation or distribution structure belongs to investment-brokerage. The employer name and contribution amount must not count for both.

An employee pay statement and an employer-wide payroll register share gross, tax, deduction and net labels. A single recipient/employee block and one covered pay period identifies a record received by that employee; multiple employee rows, a payroll-run identifier, employer totals, journal postings or remittance summaries identify the holder’s business books. One person’s row in a register does not turn the register into their personal pay statement.

falls_through_to.why: A sensitive pay, income or year-end record whose payroll series or deeper template fit is unresolved remains local-only and redacted rather than being exposed or forced into a branch.
A durable employer-issued earnings confirmation or payroll notice that lacks enough structure for this recurring situation may remain a standalone record after protection.
An isolated payment, reimbursement or deposit confirmation with no employer/employee pay-period and gross-to-net structure is transactional evidence, not a manufactured payroll history.
A confirmed screenshot whose OCR does not recover a payroll structure may use the broad screenshot residual; PNG format or missing EXIF never chooses it alone.
A partly understood foreign-language, damaged-layout or role-ambiguous earnings record can wait for local review rather than receiving invented employer, period or tax facts.
A password-protected, malformed or unsupported payroll-looking file remains safely represented from universal metadata without inferring its purpose from the filename.

sensitivity_why: This template uses the Finance safety schema, for which 00 requires: “Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains, meaning the system detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed.” Payroll also falls inside the corpus categories 00 explicitly names: “identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” Pay records contain earnings, withholding, deductions, employee identifiers and sometimes bank or benefit data, so P7 classification precedes every model path; no raw amounts or identifiers enter a cloud dossier by default. The canvas follows 00’s redaction rule: “a Finance or Identity proposal may be visible as a protected area, but the product should avoid showing sensitive filenames or sending their contents to cloud services by default.” This row records only potentially_sensitive. D2’s authoritative ClassificationRecord and P7’s handling-class value are not derived or assigned here.
open_question: R1c/Joseph has two linked merge decisions. First, should the destination-ineligible record_period proposal already shared with finance.subscriptions-utilities become a canonical fact for explicit pay, billing, statement and coverage intervals, or remain raw evidence only? Second, when one employer-issued statutory year-end form is retained in both an employer payroll history and a tax-filing packet, should P10 explicitly permit both template memberships despite also_holds_with being schema-only, or should one template own the form? This row remains usable either way: the period is not a dimension, and the year-end fixture can stay protected and reviewable without copied facts.
